claim: 1/2000 in UK have abnormal PrP positivity.
label: SUPPORT
title: Prevalent abnormal prion protein in human appendixes after bovine spongiform encephalopathy epizootic: large scale survey
rationale: RESULTS Of the 32,441 appendix samples 16 were positive for abnormal PrP, indicating an overall prevalence of 493 per million population (95% confidence interval 282 to 801 per million).

claim: AIRE is expressed in some skin tumors.
label: SUPPORT
title: Keratin-dependent regulation of Aire and gene expression in skin tumor keratinocytes
rationale: We report that autoimmune regulator (Aire), a transcriptional regulator, is inducibly expressed in human and mouse tumor keratinocytes in a K17-dependent manner and is required for timely onset of Gli2-induced skin tumorigenesis in mice.

claim: ALDH1 expression is associated with better breast cancer outcomes.
label: CONTRADICT
title: ALDH1 is a marker of normal and malignant human mammary stem cells and a predictor of poor clinical outcome.
rationale: In a series of 577 breast carcinomas, expression of ALDH1 detected by immunostaining correlated with poor prognosis.

claim: ALDH1 expression is associated with poorer prognosis in breast cancer.
label: SUPPORT
title: ALDH1 is a marker of normal and malignant human mammary stem cells and a predictor of poor clinical outcome.
rationale: In a series of 577 breast carcinomas, expression of ALDH1 detected by immunostaining correlated with poor prognosis.

claim: Activation of PPM1D suppresses p53 function.
label: SUPPORT
title: Mosaic PPM1D mutations are associated with predisposition to breast and ovarian cancer
rationale: Functional studies demonstrate that the mutations result in enhanced suppression of p53 in response to ionizing radiation exposure, suggesting that the mutant alleles encode hyperactive PPM1D isoforms.

claim: All hematopoietic stem cells segregate their chromosomes randomly.
label: SUPPORT
title: Haematopoietic stem cells do not asymmetrically segregate chromosomes or retain BrdU
rationale: Sequential administration of 5-chloro-2-deoxyuridine and 5-iodo-2-deoxyuridine indicated that all HSCs segregate their chromosomes randomly.

claim: Asymptomatic visual impairment screening in elderly populations does not lead to improved vision.
label: SUPPORT
title: Effectiveness of screening older people for impaired vision in community setting: systematic review of evidence from randomised controlled trials.
rationale: The inclusion of a visual screening component in the assessment did not result in improvements in self reported visual problems (pooled odds ratio 1.04:95% confidence interval 0.89 to 1.22). CONCLUSIONS Screening of asymptomatic older people in the community is not justified on present evidence.

claim: Autophagy declines in aged organisms.
label: SUPPORT
title: Restoration of chaperone-mediated autophagy in aging liver improves cellular maintenance and hepatic function
rationale: We have previously found that CMA activity declines in aged organisms and have proposed that this failure in cellular clearance could contribute to the accumulation of altered proteins, the abnormal cellular homeostasis and, eventually, the functional loss characteristic of aged organisms.

claim: Bariatric surgery has a positive impact on mental health.
label: SUPPORT
title: Mental Health Conditions Among Patients Seeking and Undergoing Bariatric Surgery: A Meta-analysis.
rationale: Bariatric surgery was, however, consistently associated with postoperative decreases in the prevalence of depression (7 studies; 8%-74% decrease) and the severity of depressive symptoms (6 studies; 40%-70% decrease). Moderate-quality evidence supports an association between bariatric surgery and lower rates of depression postoperatively.

claim: CHEK2 is not associated with breast cancer.
label: SUPPORT
title: Linkage Disequilibrium Mapping of       CHEK2: Common Variation and Breast Cancer Risk
rationale: We genotyped these six tagSNPs in 1,577 postmenopausal breast cancer cases and 1,513 population controls, but found no convincing association between any common CHEK2 haplotype and breast cancer risk.

claim: CX3CR1 on the Th2 cells impairs T cell survival
label: CONTRADICT
title: CX3CR1 is required for airway inflammation by promoting T helper cell survival and maintenance in inflamed lung
rationale: We found that CX3CR1 signaling promoted T(H)2 survival in the inflamed lungs, and injection of B cell leukemia/lymphoma-2 protein (BCl-2)-transduced CX3CR1-deficient T(H)2 cells into CX3CR1-deficient mice restored asthma.

claim: CX3CR1 on the Th2 cells promotes T cell survival
label: SUPPORT
title: CX3CR1 is required for airway inflammation by promoting T helper cell survival and maintenance in inflamed lung
rationale: We found that CX3CR1 signaling promoted T(H)2 survival in the inflamed lungs, and injection of B cell leukemia/lymphoma-2 protein (BCl-2)-transduced CX3CR1-deficient T(H)2 cells into CX3CR1-deficient mice restored asthma.

claim: Carriers of the alcohol aldehyde dehydrogenase deficiency mutation drink less that non-carries.
label: SUPPORT
title: Alcohol Intake and Blood Pressure: A Systematic Review Implementing a Mendelian Randomization Approach
rationale: Individuals homozygous for the null variant (*2*2) experience adverse symptoms when drinking alcohol and consequently drink considerably less alcohol than wild-type homozygotes (*1*1) or heterozygotes.

claim: Combination nicotine replacement therapies with varenicline or bupropion lead to significantly higher long-term abstinence rates at 52 weeks than varenicline monotherapy.
label: CONTRADICT
title: Combination varenicline and bupropion SR for tobacco-dependence treatment in cigarette smokers: a randomized trial.
rationale: At 52 weeks, 30.9% of the combination therapy group achieved prolonged and 36.6% achieved 7-day point-prevalence smoking abstinence compared with 24.5% and 29.2% in varenicline monotherapy (OR, 1.39; 95% CI, 0.93-2.07; P = .11 and OR, 1.40; 95% CI, 0.96-2.05; P = .08, respectively). Neither outcome was significantly different at 52 weeks.

claim: Commelina yellow mottle virus' (ComYMV) genome consists of 7489 baise pairs.
label: SUPPORT
title: Properties of Commelina yellow mottle virus's complete DNA sequence, genomic discontinuities and transcript suggest that it is a pararetrovirus.
rationale: Analysis of the genome sequence indicates that the genome is 7489 bp in size and that the transcribed strand contains three open reading frames capable of encoding proteins of 23, 15 and 216 kd.

claim: Cytochrome c is released from the mitochondrial intermembrane space to cytosol during apoptosis.
label: SUPPORT
title: At the gates of death.
rationale: Apoptosis that proceeds via the mitochondrial pathway involves mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization (MOMP), responsible for the release of cytochrome c and other proteins of the mitochondrial intermembrane space.

claim: Deletion of αvβ8 does not result in a spontaneous inflammatory phenotype.
label: SUPPORT
title: Integrin αvβ8-Mediated TGF-β Activation by Effector Regulatory T Cells Is Essential for Suppression of T-Cell-Mediated Inflammation
rationale: Treg-cell-specific deletion of integrin αvβ8 did not result in a spontaneous inflammatory phenotype, suggesting that this pathway is not important in Treg-cell-mediated maintenance of immune homeostasis.

claim: Enhanced early production of inflammatory chemokines improves viral control in the lung.
label: SUPPORT
title: Memory CD4+ T cells induce innate responses independently of pathogen
rationale: We found that the response of memory, but not naive, CD4+ T cells enhances production of multiple innate inflammatory cytokines and chemokines (IICs) in the lung and that, during influenza infection, this leads to early control of virus.

claim: Errors in peripheral IV drug administration are most common during bolus administration and multiple-step medicine preparations.
label: SUPPORT
title: Ethnographic study of incidence and severity of intravenous drug errors.
rationale: Most errors occurred when giving bolus doses or making up drugs that required multiple step preparation. A combination of reducing the amount of preparation on the ward, training, and technology to administer slow bolus doses would probably have the greatest effect on error rates.

claim: High cardiopulmonary fitness causes increased mortality rate.
label: CONTRADICT
title: Prevalence and cardiovascular disease correlates of low cardiorespiratory fitness in adolescents and adults.
rationale: CONCLUSION Low fitness in adolescents and adults is common in the US population and is associated with an increased prevalence of CVD risk factors.

claim: The US health care system can save up to $750 million if 7% of patients waiting for kidney transplants participate in the optimized national kidney paired donation program.
label: SUPPORT
title: Kidney paired donation and optimizing the use of live donor organs.
rationale: Even if only 7% of patients awaiting kidney transplantation participated in an optimized national KPD program, the health care system could save as much as $750 million.

claim: 76-85% of people with severe mental disorder receive no treatment in low and middle income countries.
label: SUPPORT
title: Prevalence, severity, and unmet need for treatment of mental disorders in the World Health Organization World Mental Health Surveys.
rationale: Although disorder severity was correlated with probability of treatment in almost all countries, 35.5% to 50.3% of serious cases in developed countries and 76.3% to 85.4% in less-developed countries received no treatment in the 12 months before the interview.

claim: In British Men, haplogroup I increases risk of cardiovascular disease by 50%.
label: SUPPORT
title: Inheritance of coronary artery disease in men: an analysis of the role of the Y chromosome
rationale: Carriers of haplogroup I had about a 50% higher age-adjusted risk of coronary artery disease than did men with other Y chromosome lineages in BHF-FHS (odds ratio 1·75, 95% CI 1·20-2·54, p=0·004), WOSCOPS (1·45, 1·08-1·95, p=0·012), and joint analysis of both populations (1·56, 1·24-1·97, p=0·0002).

claim: Nonhypertensive people who are 55 years old have a 90% chance of developing hypertension during their lifetime.
label: SUPPORT
title: Residual lifetime risk for developing hypertension in middle-aged women and men: The Framingham Heart Study.
rationale: RESULTS The residual lifetime risks for developing hypertension and stage 1 high blood pressure or higher (greater-than-or-equal to 140/90 mm Hg regardless of treatment) were 90% in both 55- and 65-year-old participants. CONCLUSION The residual lifetime risk for hypertension for middle-aged and elderly individuals is 90%, indicating a huge public health burden.

claim: Participants who quit smoking reduce lung cancer risk by approximately 50%.
label: SUPPORT
title: Effect of smoking reduction on lung cancer risk.
rationale: The HR for light smokers was 0.44 (95% CI, 0.35-0.56); for quitters, HR 0.50 (95% CI, 0.36-0.69), for stable ex-smokers, HR 0.17 (95% CI, 0.13-0.23), and for never smokers, HR 0.09 (95% CI, 0.06-0.13).

claim: Ten percent (10%) of kidney cancers in the UK are attributable to excess weight.
label: SUPPORT
title: Body-mass index and risk of 22 specific cancers: a population-based cohort study of 5·24 million UK adults
rationale: Assuming causality, 41% of uterine and 10% or more of gallbladder, kidney, liver, and colon cancers could be attributable to excess weight.

claim: There was an estimated 30 million cases of pneumonia in young children worldwide in 2010.
label: SUPPORT
title: Global and regional burden of hospital admissions for severe acute lower respiratory infections in young children in 2010: a systematic analysis
rationale: FINDINGS We identified 89 eligible studies and estimated that in 2010, 11·9 million (95% CI 10·3-13·9 million) episodes of severe and 3·0 million (2·1-4·2 million) episodes of very severe ALRI resulted in hospital admissions in young children worldwide.
